tagline: A loop through the panhandle, following the Washingtons to the springs.
intro: From Harpers Ferry, where the Shenandoah meets the Potomac, the trail loops west through Charles Town, Shepherdstown and Martinsburg to the old spa town of Berkeley Springs, going out by one branch and coming back by another. From the springs a spur follows WV 9 west past Panorama Overlook, where Cacapon Mountain drops nearly 1,000 feet to the Potomac, to Paw Paw.

It follows the Washingtons. George first came to the springs at sixteen and kept coming back. His brother Charles founded Charles Town, and at Harewood, the gray limestone house of his brother Samuel, Dolley Payne Todd married James Madison in 1794.

moments.title: Jefferson Rock, Harpers Ferry
moments.text: Up the old stone stairs above St. Peter's Church, Jefferson stood here in 1783 to see the two rivers cut through the Blue Ridge, and judged it worth a voyage across the Atlantic.

moments.title: George Washington's Bathtub, Berkeley Springs
moments.text: The country's only outdoor monument to presidential bathing, a stone tub rebuilt in the 1930s with a spring bubbling up through it.

moments.title: Paw Paw Tunnel
moments.text: Six million bricks line this 3,118-foot canal tunnel, opened in 1850, fourteen years late and just in time for the railroad to make the canal obsolete.

practical: Paw Paw Tunnel is across the Potomac in Maryland, reached from MD 51 by the canal towpath. Sturdy shoes and a flashlight are recommended. Harewood is a private home, and visitors may photograph it only from the driveway.
